target.title: fix (Computer Use) Stabilize Codex Computer Use readiness
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Codex Computer Use readiness could go stale or look healthy when it was not actually usable. OpenClaw agents can run with isolated per-agent `CODEX_HOME` directories, so one agent could keep a stale cached Computer Use plugin even after the locally installed Codex.app bundle was updated. Status/setup also reported coarse plugin availability without separately proving installation, MCP exposure, and live `list_apps` behavior.

That is how a request could ask for Codex Computer Use while the runtime silently lacked a working Computer Use bridge or fell back to other automation without making the failure inspectable.

## Summary

This PR hardens Codex Computer Use setup so OpenClaw no longer treats “plugin exists somewhere” as sufficient readiness.

It adds:

- shared local bundled Computer Use plugin cache reconciliation for per-agent `CODEX_HOME` directories, defaulting to a real copied cache entry that Codex can discover and removing stale cached versions
- decomposed `/codex computer-use status` results for installation, MCP exposure, and a live `computer-use.list_apps` probe
- 60s live-probe timeout, exactly one 60s retry, and opt-in narrow auto-repair that only terminates stale `SkyComputerUseClient ... mcp` children when `computerUse.autoRepair` is true
- opt-in periodic per-shared-client Computer Use health probes when `computerUse.healthCheckEnabled` is true, using the configured 30/60/120/240 minute cadence and the same live-probe path
- fail-closed setup behavior by default while keeping browser/DOM fallback available when explicitly requested outside the Computer Use setup path
- config/schema/docs for `liveTestTimeoutMs`, `toolCallTimeoutMs`, `leaseTimeoutMs`, `healthCheckEnabled`, `healthCheckIntervalMinutes`, `pluginCacheMode`, `fallbackOnFailure`, and `autoRepair`
- a window-scope Computer Use lease manager with renewal/preemption semantics for callers that can supply a stable window id
- `openclaw doctor` surfacing for enabled Codex Computer Use, including configured health cadence and the status command to inspect installation/exposure/live-test layers

## Context

This addresses the failure mode where one OpenClaw agent could keep using a stale per-agent Codex plugin cache even after Codex.app had a newer bundled Computer Use plugin, and where status/setup could report only coarse plugin availability instead of separating install state, MCP exposure, and live runtime health.

The previous direction in #96730 improved app-server command selection/startup behavior, but it did not make Computer Use readiness globally inspectable across agents, did not reconcile isolated per-agent plugin caches with the locally installed Codex.app bundle, and did not prove the MCP bridge with a real `list_apps` call before reporting readiness. This PR closes those gaps locally and offline; it does not depend on a remote marketplace.

## Notes

The new lease manager is window-scoped by design, not app-scoped and not host-global. Native Codex MCP notifications are observational, so full pre-execution enforcement requires Computer Use tool payloads to expose a stable window identifier before the MCP call begins. The PR documents that boundary and adds the tested lease primitive for call sites that can provide that scope.

## Evidence

Post-repair exact head: `10e644c505144bf4d4d9ded034761be19f542e6c` rebased on `origin/main` `9f248969f6c81141f8a513cb8b9209fe09d29b33`.

Focused checks rerun after the cache/probe repair and final rebase:

- `git diff --check`
- `node scripts/generate-docs-map.mjs --check`
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 extensions/codex/src/app-server/computer-use-cache.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/computer-use-cache.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/sandbox-guard.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/request.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/request.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/computer-use.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/computer-use.test.ts`
- `PNPM_CONFIG_VERIFY_DEPS_BEFORE_RUN=false node scripts/test-extension.mjs codex extensions/codex/src/app-server/computer-use.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/computer-use-cache.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/computer-use-health.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/computer-use-leases.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/config.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/request.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/attempt-startup.test.ts extensions/codex/src/commands.test.ts` — 8 files / 301 tests passed
- `PNPM_CONFIG_VERIFY_DEPS_BEFORE_RUN=false node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.commands.config.ts src/commands/doctor/shared/codex-route-warnings.test.ts` — 1 file / 112 tests passed
- `PNPM_CONFIG_VERIFY_DEPS_BEFORE_RUN=false node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/extensions-test.tsbuildinfo`
- `PNPM_CONFIG_VERIFY_DEPS_BEFORE_RUN=false node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.src.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/test-src.tsbuildinfo`
- `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD` equals `HEAD^{tree}` (`12238460fb992227f876bf5118ae8bb0029b8fc6`)

Repair-specific coverage added:

- explicit `computerUse.marketplaceName` and `computerUse.marketplacePath` cache namespaces are skipped by shared cache reconciliation and preserved as-is
- sandbox direct-MCP probe bypass now requires `computerUseMcpServerName` and only permits that configured server's `list_apps`
- live Computer Use proof rerun on current `codex` app-server with a temporary local Computer Use marketplace
